note: Original classroom practice. Independent academic review pending.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish an agreed script from dialogue invented during performance.
questions.prompt: A teacher tells two actors that they are returning a borrowed drum. The teacher gives them a situation and asks them to invent their lines as they perform. Which category describes this scene?
questions.explanation: The situation is given, while the dialogue is created during the scene. That is improvisation.
options: A reading of a prepared script.
A rehearsal of a fixed speech.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Identify the work of production personnel in a school drama.
questions.prompt: A scene needs a bench, a basket and a letter. Who should check that these objects are ready and placed for the actors to use?
questions.explanation: The bench, basket and letter are props. Their preparation and placement belong to the props role.
options: The actor who plays the narrator in an unrelated scene.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Perform a short scene using purposeful voice, movement and cues.
questions.prompt: With a partner, act a short scene in which two pupils realise they have prepared different versions of an announcement. Let the audience see the discovery through movement. Use one spoken line as a cue for your partner and end with a shared decision.
questions.answer: One actor unfolds a page and points to a time. The other compares a second page and says, “Wait, our times are different.” The first actor responds by turning both pages towards the audience. They agree to check the approved notice before speaking.
questions.explanation: Movement makes the discovery visible. The cue links the actors’ actions, and the decision gives the scene an ending.

markingGuide.description: Shows the discovery through a clear physical action.
Uses an audible line that prompts the partner’s response.
Responds to the partner’s cue in character.
Ends with a clear shared decision.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Perform a short scene using purposeful voice, movement and cues.
questions.prompt: Perform a solo scene at a school exhibition. Begin as a guide who thinks a display is ready, then discover that a label has fallen. Use posture and voice to show the change. Finish by explaining to an imagined visitor what will happen next.
questions.answer: The guide begins upright with an even voice, pauses and bends to notice the fallen label, then speaks more deliberately: “Please give me a moment to put this label back beside the correct work.”
questions.explanation: A visible and audible change helps viewers follow the guide’s reaction before the final explanation.

markingGuide.description: Establishes the guide’s role and the setting.
Uses a clear change in posture after the discovery.
Uses an audible change in voice that suits the situation.
Concludes with a clear explanation to the imagined visitor.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Create and perform a short percussion pattern while maintaining a regular pulse.
questions.prompt: Using a teacher-provided hand drum or shaker, create a four-beat pattern with at least one rest. Perform it three times at a steady pace. Before starting, tell the examiner which beat has the rest.
questions.answer: One possible pattern is sound, sound, rest, sound. Repeat it three times, keeping the silent third beat as long as each sounding beat.
questions.explanation: Keeping time during the rest preserves the four-beat pattern. Other original patterns meeting the constraints are valid.

markingGuide.description: Creates a four-beat pattern with an intentional rest.
States the location of the rest correctly.
Maintains an even pulse through sound and silence.
Repeats the same pattern three times.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Create and perform a short percussion pattern while maintaining a regular pulse.
questions.prompt: With a partner and two teacher-provided percussion instruments, make a four-beat musical exchange. One pupil plays a short call in the first two beats and the other answers in the last two. Repeat the full exchange twice and finish together with a silent hand signal.
questions.answer: For example, the first player taps once on each of beats one and two. The second taps on beat three and leaves beat four silent. Both maintain the pulse for a second exchange, then give the agreed stop signal.
questions.explanation: The exchange works when the response begins on the planned beat and both performers agree when to finish.

markingGuide.description: Creates distinguishable call and response parts.
Places the call and response in the agreed beat positions.
Repeats the exchange without losing the pulse.
Coordinates the agreed finish with the partner.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Identify changes in tempo and dynamics from a short described performance.
questions.prompt: A group sings the same phrase twice. The second time, the beats occur at the same speed but the singers are noticeably quieter. Which feature changed?
questions.explanation: Dynamics describe loudness and softness. The question states that the beat speed stayed the same.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Compose and sing a short original phrase using a regular pulse and planned contrast.
questions.prompt: Make up two short lines for a class clean-up song. Sing them over a steady beat. Keep the second line softer than the first and repeat the two lines once using the same tune.
questions.answer: Example words: “Stack the books and clear the way / Leave the room ready for today.” A successful performance uses a short singable tune, a steady beat, and a softer second line on both passes.
questions.explanation: Repeating the tune preserves the composition. The planned dynamic contrast adds expression without requiring a change in speed.

markingGuide.description: Creates two original lines about the activity.
Sings a recognisable tune and repeats it.
Keeps a steady underlying pulse.
Makes the second line audibly softer on both passes.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Draw a five-line stave and distinguish lines from spaces.
questions.prompt: Draw one musical stave on plain paper. Label the bottom line as line 1, then shade only the second space from the bottom. Explain how you counted.
questions.answer: Draw five horizontal parallel lines. Count lines upwards from the bottom, then shade the gap between lines 2 and 3.
questions.explanation: The five lines enclose four spaces. The first space sits between the first and second lines, so the next gap is the second space.

markingGuide.description: Draws five approximately parallel lines.
Labels the bottom line correctly.
Shades the gap between lines 2 and 3.
Explains the counting direction or the two adjacent lines.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Place named notes on their correct lines or spaces in the treble stave.
questions.prompt: On a teacher-provided blank treble stave, place a notehead for G on its line inside the stave and a notehead for A on the space immediately above it. Write the line and space numbers, counting from the bottom.
questions.answer: G goes on line 2 and A goes in space 2, between lines 2 and 3.
questions.explanation: The treble clef identifies the second line as G. The next position above it is the second space, A.

markingGuide.description: Places G on the second line.
Places A in the second space.
Labels the two positions accurately.
